chunks: Everything in this book that is narrated from Hanan ibn Sudayr has been transmitted by me from my father, and from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan (may Allah be pleased with them both) from Sa'd ibn Abdullah, and Abdullah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari together, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Hanan. And I have transmitted it from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan (may Allah be pleased with him) from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Saffar, from Abdul-Samad ibn Muhammad, from Hanan. And I have transmitted it from Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh (may Allah be pleased with him) from Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from Hanan ibn Sudayr.

key_terms.حَنَانِ بْنِ سُدَيْرٍ: Hanan ibn Sudayr, a prominent narrator of hadith
key_terms.سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Sa'd ibn Abdullah, a key narrator
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عِيسَى: Muhammad ibn Isa, a narrator in the chain

ai.seo_question: How is the authenticity of Hanan ibn Sudayr's narrations verified in this text?
ai.summary: This passage exemplifies the rigorous methodology of *al-Saduq* in verifying the authenticity of narrations by cross-referencing multiple independent chains of transmission (*tawatur*) for Hanan ibn Sudayr. By citing his own direct transmissions alongside those of prominent scholars like Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar and Majilawayh, the text underscores the reliability of the Kufi school of hadith and provides a model for establishing the credibility of individual narrators within Shia jurisprudence.
